verses.1: So, six days after the Passion, Jesus went to Bethany, where Lazarus was lying dead. Jesus raised him from the dead.
verses.2: They therefore prepared food for him there. Martha served the food, while Lazarus was one of those who stayed with him.
verses.3: So, when Mary took the jar of expensive perfume, she smelled it and rubbed her feet against Jesus’ feet. As a result, the house was filled with the scent of that perfume.
verses.4: And Iudas the Iskariote said among his disciples, “One of them will betray him.”
verses.5: Why wasn’t this milled into three hundred denarii, and given to the poor?
verses.6: He said this not only because he cared about the poor, but also because he was a thief who stole things from others and used those stolen items for his own purposes.
verses.7: So Jesus said, “Behold, I will make her hold this until the day of my burial.”
verses.8: For you always have the poor with you, but you don’t always have me with you.
verses.9: So, the crowd was very surprised to find that He was there. They didn’t come just because of Jesus alone, but also to see Lazarus, who had been raised from the dead.
verses.10: But the high priests decided to also kill Lazarus as well.
verses.11: Because many Jews came to him and believed in Jesus.
verses.12: In the evening, when the crowd arrived at the feast, they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
verses.13: We took the crowns of the priests and went before him. We cried out loudly, “Hosanna!” For he was indeed blessed, coming in the name of the Lord. And he was the king of Israel.
verses.14: And when Jesus found him, he sat down beside him, as it was written.
verses.15: Do not fear, daughter of Sion. Look, your king is coming, seated on a mule.
verses.16: The disciples didn’t know these things at first. But when Jesus became famous, they remembered that these things had been written about him, and that he had done them.
verses.17: Thus, the crowd testified when they heard Lazarus speak from the tomb and call him out of the dead.
verses.18: For this reason, the crowd also told him that they believed he had heard this as a sign.
verses.19: So the Pharisees said to themselves, “It seems that nothing is useful at all.” Look, the world has gone back to its old ways again.
verses.20: And there were some Greeks among those who were coming along, who wanted to worship them during the festival.
verses.21: These men then went to Philip from Bethsaida in Galilee. They asked him, “Lord, we want to see Jesus.”
verses.22: Philip comes and says to Andrew. Andrew comes, and Philip also comes, and they say these things to Jesus.
verses.23: But Jesus replied to them, “The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.”
verses.24: I say to you, indeed, if the seed of the bean does not fall into the soil and die, then it remains alone. But if it does die, it brings forth many seeds.
verses.25: Those who love his soul will preserve her; those who hate his soul will keep her alive in this world for eternal life.
verses.26: If someone serves me, and he follows me wherever I go, then he will also be my servant. If anyone serves me with respect, his father will honor him accordingly.
verses.27: Now, my soul is troubled. What can I say? Father, save me from this world. But it’s because of this that we have come to this world.
verses.28: Father, may your name be glorified. Then a voice came from heaven; and it was glorified once more. I will also glorify it again.
verses.29: So, the crowd, when they heard this, said that it was a miracle. Others said, “It’s just a dream.” But the angel spoke to them.
verses.30: Jesus replied, “It wasn’t my voice that spoke, but your voices.”
verses.31: Now, this world’s ruler will be brought to trial. Now, he who rules over this world will be exposed to judgment.
verses.32: If I were to rise above the earth, I would bring everyone together with me.
verses.33: This, however, meant that he was about to die of a natural death.
verses.34: So, the crowd said to him, “We have heard from the law that Christ will remain in heaven forever. How can you say that the Son of Man must be raised from the dead? Who is this Son of Man?”
verses.35: Then Jesus said to them, “Yet a little while, the light in you is still present. Walk as if you had light within you, so that darkness cannot overpower you. And those who walk in darkness do not know where they are going.”
verses.36: As you believe in the light, so do you believe that it will give birth to children who are also lights. This is what Jesus said. After saying this, he left from them.
verses.37: But so many of his signs were not believed by those who saw them before him; they did not believe in him at all.
verses.38: So that the words of the prophet Esai might be fulfilled. “Lord, who has deceived our ears?” And what was revealed to the king Belshazzar?
verses.39: Therefore, they could not believe that Esaias had spoken again.
verses.40: He made their eyes blind, and he deprived them of their ability to see. This was so that they would not be able to see with their eyes, but could only understand through their hearts. Then I could control them.
verses.41: These were the words that Esaias said, because he saw his glory. He spoke about him in those terms.
verses.42: However, still, many of the leaders believed in him. But they didn’t admit it out of fear that they might be accused of being part of a conspiracy.
verses.43: For they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God.
verses.44: But Jesus cried out and said, “He who believes in me, believes not in me but in the one who sent me.”
verses.45: And he who considers me to be a god, he also considers those who sent me to be gods.
verses.46: I have brought light to the world, so that everyone who believes in me may not be left in darkness.
verses.47: And if anyone hears my words but doesn’t follow them, I don’t judge him. After all, I wasn’t sent here to judge the world, but to save it.
verses.48: He who despises me and refuses to take my words into consideration, has himself as his judge. The words I spoke were judged by him on that last day.
verses.49: Because I did not speak on my own authority; rather, it was my father who gave me instructions about what to say and what not to say.
verses.50: And I know that his command is eternal. What I say, I say as my father has commanded me to say.
